banner: **Discovery inventory, not a result.** It lists mathematical artifacts that were delivered inside GitHub comments, PR reviews and issue/PR descriptions, with where their bytes are committed and what implements them. It makes no correctness claim and no CLOSED/QUARANTINED disposition. Credit 0 · sci NONE · OBL OPEN.
coverage: Repositories crawled: main, Math-, governance-, google-drive, d6g8k5htny-coder, meta-framework, query-, sandbox, trial and Universal-Law-Workspace. These are all the repositories this session can read; repositories outside that set are not covered.
Issue and PR conversation comments: 37,624, from the first on 19 September to 31 October 2026 17:20Z (REST `issues/comments`, all pages).
PR review bodies and issue/PR descriptions: 3,415 non-empty items (REST `pulls/{n}/reviews` for every PR, and `issues?state=all`).

Stage A (lexical prefilter: length > 2,500, at least 3 theorem/proof/inequality markers, and RESULT/PROOF/NOTE/frozen in the first 600 characters): 1,761 candidate comments, classified one by one; 403 delivered artifacts.
Stage B (reviews and descriptions, same prefilter plus a looser band): 865 candidates; 106 artifacts. Descriptions that only summarize files the PR commits are not counted separately.
Recall audit of stage A: 160 comments drawn at random (seed 20261031) from the 10,619 excluded comments that are over 800 characters and carry a math marker. 7 delivered mathematics (4.4%).

Stage C: because of that audit, all 10,619 excluded comments were triaged by agents (recall-oriented, full bodies opened when ambiguous). 948 were flagged and every flag fully classified; 436 artifacts. Of the 7 audit positives, 6 were recovered by stage C.

Residual: 22,675 non-bot comments are outside stages A and C (at most 800 characters, or no math marker). A uniform sample of 200 (seed 1031) found 1 artifact, so roughly 0.5% of the residual (on the order of 100 comments, with a wide interval) may carry mathematics this census does not list.
Artifacts are deduplicated by key; later versions or mirrors of the same key are listed as extra comment versions on one row.
limits: Classification and custody are model-assisted judgments by Anthropic Claude subagents of this session, with independence credit 0. Each row keeps the custody agent's evidence note. They can be wrong.

Every listed carrier (repository, commit, path, blob) is checked mechanically by verify_census.py. COMMITTED_ON_MAIN means at least one cited blob is in the main or Math- tree at the cut; copy_kind says whether the evidence describes a byte-identical copy, an incorporation (restated or credited in a committed file), or neither.

INLINE_ONLY means the custody searches found no committed copy. The inline probe re-checks this mechanically: distinctive comment lines are searched at the cuts, and two or more in one committed file reclassify the row. A probe cannot prove absence.
Drive and Dropbox were not searched for bytes; DRIVE_OR_DROPBOX_ONLY_CITED only records what the post cites.
Comments can be edited after the cut. Each version records the body SHA-256 at read time; `verify_census.py --live` reports drift.

The records column is recomputed by git grep at the cuts over docs/retro/, the coverage ledger, cbz/, docs/cbz/, STATUS.md and the Workspace INVENTORY files, for the comment id, the artifact key and committed carrier paths. A mention of a packet path counts as a mention.
No CLOSED or QUARANTINED disposition is made here; that is the proof-closure role's. For Math- packets, the claude54_packets field cross-references Claude 54's packet ledger at Math- 8151f592.
Anthropic-authored artifacts, including this author's, are listed structurally like every other row and are not judged.

Audit (2 November): a stratified random sample of 50 rows (seed 20261101; 16 INLINE_ONLY, 14 COMMITTED_ON_MAIN, 10 COMMITTED_ON_BRANCH_ONLY, 5 DRIVE_OR_DROPBOX_ONLY_CITED, plus 3 NONE_FOUND and 2 NONE_NEEDED implementation rows), drawn from the 827 rows complete at 23:30Z on 1 November, was re-checked by subagents told to refute each classification. Each dispute went to an adjudicator, and a value changed only when a second adjudicator independently reached the same replacement. 50 of 50 rows returned. custody: 44 agreed, 5 corrected, 1 disputed but upheld, 0 disputed and unresolved; implementation: 45 agreed, 5 corrected, 0 disputed but upheld, 0 disputed and unresolved; statement: 47 agreed, 3 corrected, 0 disputed but upheld, 0 disputed and unresolved. Corrections were applied to sampled rows only; unsampled rows carry the same error rate in expectation. The auditors and adjudicators are Anthropic Claude subagents of this session (independence credit 0); each sampled row's `audit` field records its outcome.

Citation pass (2 November): every gap-list row outside the audit sample whose comment id appears in a committed main or Math- file at the cut (119 rows) was re-checked by a subagent that opened those files; a row moved to COMMITTED_ON_MAIN only when a second agent independently agreed that a file carries the mathematics. 34 rows were promoted, 85 only cite the comment, 0 split and were kept, 0 did not return. The other gap rows have no committed main or Math- file citing their comment id; a credited restatement that cites only an issue number or a key would not be found this way (the audit found one such case).

artifacts.statement: SIDE24-PINNED-GENERICITY-20260924-v1. For the exact normalized SIDE24 field, any fixed distinct M,S and six pins (fM,fxM,fyM,fS,fxS,fyS)=(b,0,0,b-ell,0,0) with ell>0, the Gaussian regression law Q is supported on Morse functions with distinct critical values. Also 0<Z=E_Q W<inf for W=|det H_M det H_S|1{M maximum, S saddle}, and the full-probability locus transfers to Q^W=(W/Z)Q by absolute continuity. The body gives only a proof path: positive weights on every torus Fourier mode, then independent finite jets, then conditional Schur positivity modulo the pins, then an overdetermined-zero covering lemma. Degenerate unpinned critical points use the map (grad f, Hf v) (range 4, domain 3); equal critical values use the two-point gradient/value-difference map (range 5, domain 4); pinned Hessians and ties to the pinned heights are handled separately. Covariance lower bounds are local compact-set existence statements. It reuses the Morse-only definition of CL-DER-MEAS-20260727-01.

artifacts.statement: Fixed-r inverse-moment obstruction (same law). For every eps>=0, Q_r^W(0<s_M<=eps)<=min(1,(45/544)eps^3+(789/2176)r*eps^2). For each fixed r>0, exact disintegration gives Q_r^W(s_M<=eps)=kappa_r*eps^2+o(eps^2) with kappa_r>0, because the scalar density is (r^2/Z)*s*F_r(s) with F_r(0)>0. So E_Q^W[s_M^-p] is finite exactly for 0<p<2, with bound 1+p(45/544)/(3-p)+p(789/2176)r/(2-p), and infinite for p>=2 (logarithmic at p=2). The contact-limit weighted density s^2 p_T(-s)/z0 has finite inverse moments for p<3. So for 2<=p<3 the limiting moment is finite while every finite-r moment is infinite, and weak convergence cannot justify that moment transfer. Companion warning: with the unscaled physical Hessian, Q^W(lambda_min(-H_M)<=2r) tends to 1, because the axial fold mode is already soft.

artifacts.statement: Whole-square critical isolation and local preemption bounds, same fixed-axis 2D SIDE24 six-pin law, 0<r<=1/20. (A) Let H(r)=25+8sqrt(12log(1/r)+16) and rho(r)=r/[64H(r)]. With Q^W-probability >1-4r^3, both closed endpoint balls of radius rho(r) have constant Hessian inertia, smallest singular value >r/16 and no other critical point, and |grad f(i+h)|>=(r/16)|h|. At r=1/20, 0.0000094513<rho<0.0000094514. (B) On D_r=[-2r,2r]^2, Q^W(E_extra ∪ E_path)<=min(1,C3 r^3+C4 r^4)<=min(1,1.3e26 r^3). (C) Under the LPW witness premises, [13/468574870385996070912000]r^3<=Q^W(E_path)<=1.3e26 r^3 for 0<r<=1/356352 (local path event only). Main argument: peel off q=fyy(M) by regression so the residual field is jointly independent of q, and build T>=1 with ||T||_8<320. The conditions -q>64r(1+M3)^2 and rM4<=1/20 force fyy<0 on D_r and a unique transverse-critical ridge whose reduced derivative has F''>1 and exactly two zeros. The column through S then blocks above-saddle preemption paths. The failure set lies in 0<-q<=256rT^2 or |q|>1/(16384r). Integration gives r^5/Z, i.e. r^3. Anchored infinite dyadic chaining controls third and fourth derivative suprema.

artifacts.statement: P15-B matroid palette specialization. If the independent sets of the complete crossing-support hypergraph form a loopless matroid M, then K*=max over nonempty A⊆[n] of ceil(sum_{i in A} d_i / rank_M(A)). Lower bound: each color contributes at most rank(A) incidences in A. Upper bound: replace each block i by d_i parallel color-demand copies, so that |U|<=K*rank_M(supp U), then apply Edmonds' matroid partition theorem (J. Res. NBS 69B, 1965, Thm 1). A maximizing A gives dual weights y_i=1/rank(A); the fractional optimum is R and the integral optimum is ceil(R). Uniform rank: if all (rank+1)-subsets are crossing supports, K*=max(max_i d_i, ceil(sum_i d_i/rank)), realized by consecutive cyclic demand segments. Witness: six blocks of demand 408 with all 15 four-block supports give K*=816 (408 labels on {0,2,4} and 408 others on {1,3,5}; lower bound 2448/3=816), against 2448 for disjoint palettes.

artifacts.statement: The six-pin cubic is f = r^3[2k u^3-(3k/2)u-k/2+(q/2)(u^2-1/4)v+(A/2+cu/2)v^2+(d/6)v^3] + lambda(x^2-r^2/4)^2 with a = A-c/2, the witness at X = M + r^2(P,Q), and Q != 0. Solving both finite-r witness equations f_x(X) = f_z(X) = 0 exactly gives closed forms for q(r) and a(r), with first coefficients q0 = -12kP/Q, a0 = -6kP^2/Q^2, q1 = -12kP^2/Q + cQ + 4lambda P/Q and a1 = -(cP+dQ)/2 + 2lambda P^2/Q^2. Then [r^3] det H_M = -6k a1 + 2lambda a0 - q0 q1/2 = 9kcP + 3kdQ - 72k^2 P^3/Q^2, and all lambda terms cancel. So QUARTIC section 2's -12 lambda k P^2 r^3/Q^2, which uses the leading-only substitution, is not the finite-witness constrained factor. Exact counterexample with k=P=Q=1, c=d=lambda=0 and 0<r<1/2: q = -12(1-r)/(1-2r), A = -6(1-r)^2/(1-2r), det H_M = -72 r^3 (1-r)^2/(1-2r)^2 != 0. This pure cubic satisfies all six endpoint pins and both witness pins, with no quartic. Substituting only q=-12, A=-6 leaves f_x(X) = f_z(X) = -6r^4. The post includes the full stdlib Fraction script inline with its expected transcript.

artifacts.statement: Derivation outline of a sharpened C6 factorial-moment bound. Quantitative growth: E_{Q_r} sup_{Omega_R(c)} |grad f|^2 <= C exp(C R^2), uniformly in the pin family, via Minkowski on sum sqrt(a_n)|n|^k exp(R|n|), completing the square, and the bounded E_r regression rows and inverse. Take the Taylor Cauchy radius R_m = R0 sqrt(m) instead of 4eta'. Then on the fixed test spheres rho <= 2eta' the remainder factor is a_m <= C0^m m^(-m/2). Cutoffs: lambda_m = m^(m/16), epsilon_m = 2 lambda_m a_m, delta_m = epsilon_m / lambda_m. The packing/Markov term is <= exp(Cm) m^(-m/4) O(m log m), and the S_m tail is exp(Cm) m^(-m/8). These give P(m* > m) <= C exp(-c m log m) (current bound exp(-cm)) and P(Psi > x) <= C exp(-c sqrt(x) log x). Choosing x ~ [log(1/r)/loglog(1/r)]^2 gives E N(N-1) <= C r^3 [log(1/r)/loglog(1/r)]^2, with the analogous 2(q-1) exponent, for small r.

artifacts.statement: Review of #145 §4 with new mathematics. (1) An alternative proof of Lemma 4.3 that needs no comparison theorem. After any finite Gaussian regression, each centered residual Fourier coordinate has variance at most its prior variance and Lp norm at most C_p times the prior spectral standard deviation. Minkowski on the fixed complex tube then controls every derivative supremum, since sum sqrt(a_n)|n|^j exp(Y|n|) < ∞. The bound is uniform in the regressing frame and needs neither residual independence nor a uniform inverse Gram matrix. (2) An arithmetic repair. eta'/(2delta) - zeta0/delta - 1 >= eta'/(4delta) does not follow from zeta0 <= eta'/4 and delta <= eta'/8 alone. It does hold using the actual cover's stronger ratio zeta0 = eta/64 <= eta'/8 (smallest eta' = eta/8). (3) A Lemma D' convention: if phi=0, set Phi=∞, so the bounds become vacuous and applications must prove Phi finite. (4) A witness-lift convention: fix the lift per chart, or use the distance to the full torus lift set. At most one lift lies near the compact ball.

artifacts.statement: Refutes and corrects the #159 v1.1 §8 claim that extra in-window critical points may be maxima or saddles, both with positive weight. On the typed cubic domain, every extra critical point with height strictly in (-k,0) is a saddle. In sheared coordinates det Hess = -3k(B+4su). For B<0 the window forces u < -1/2, so B+4su > B-2s > 0. For B>0 it forces -1/2 < u < -1/2 - B/(2s), so B+4su > -B-2s > 0. For B=0 only u = -1/2 can be in-window, and the determinant is 6ks < 0. artifacts.statement: Fixed-r upper route matching the Schur/Taylor lower bound. Take a C^3 field with H_M<0, lambda=lambda_min(-H_M), K>=1+||H_M||+||D^3 f||_inf and a_L=min(1,L/4). On the sphere R=a_L lambda/K, Taylor gives f<=b-lambda R^2/3, so every finite actual lifetime satisfies ell>=c_L lambda^3/K^2. Conditioning on both full Hessians gives E[K^2|H_M,H_S]<=C_r(1+||H_M||+||H_S||)^m. With the original maximum determinant kept, the soft-eigenvalue integral for ell<=eps is bounded by C_r int_0^1 lambda min(1,eps/lambda^3) d lambda + O_r(eps), and with eps=s^3 that integral is exactly (3/2)s^2-s^3. Hence Q_r^W(0<ell<=eps)<=C_r eps^{2/3}. With the lower bound this gives Q_r^W(0<ell<=eps)=Theta_r(eps^{2/3}). So the finite-death inverse-moment threshold is exactly 2/3, capped critical inverse moments grow like Theta_r(log T), and supercritical ones like Theta_r(T^{p-2/3}).

artifacts.statement: Logarithmic endpoint corollary. Let Y=Delta/ell on a finite-death event A, with Y=0 off A, so that P(Y>t)=Theta_r(t^{-2/3}) by (18). Let h_beta(y)=y^{2/3}/(log y)^beta for y>=y0, with log y0>=max(1,3|beta|). Then h_beta'(y)=y^{-1/3}(log y)^{-beta}[2/3-beta/log y], and the bracket is bounded between positive constants. Layer-cake integration gives E[h_beta(Y);Y>=y0]<inf iff beta>1. The capped expectation grows like Theta_r(log log T) at beta=1 and like Theta_r((log T)^{1-beta}) for beta<1. A single logarithm therefore does not make the critical inverse moment integrable.

artifacts.statement: An exact logical countermodel against NOTE.md's claim that every admissible [LP] Theorem A constant satisfies C >= c_G. Take one uniform U, F_r = {U <= r^3} and G_r^c = {U <= 2r^3} for 0 < r <= 1/2. Then F_r ⊂ G_r^c and the cap coefficient is 2, yet C = 1 is admissible for the target failure. So the asymptotic coefficient of the larger probability Q^W(G_r^c) does not lower-bound constants for the smaller one, 1 - p_r. The corrected statement is C_cap >= c_G, with C_cap defined by Q^W(G_r^c) <= C_cap r^3 ([LP] (7.8)). The post also suggests a repair: make the convergence domination explicit through the existing twelfth moment, with the expected integrand bounded by C(1+u)^2 u^-4 at large u. It also records an independent Slice A reconstruction that confirms the typed r^4 factor, the r^3 scaling, 1/(216k^3), and the variances 1/2, 2, 6.

artifacts.statement: Counterexample to the step 'smooth stationary covariance with nondegenerate conditioning implies a real-analytic Atilde' in Lemma E of Math-#231. Take the 1-d even positive spectral density w(xi) = exp(-sqrt|xi|)/4 and K(x) = int cos(x xi) w(xi) dxi. Then K is a normalized C-infinity stationary covariance (K(0) = 1) with strictly positive finite-jet Gram matrices, but |K^(2n)(0)| = Gamma(4n+2) = (4n+1)!, so its Taylor series at 0 has radius zero. The section 4 argument therefore gives only parity and formal Taylor identities, which are enough for the finite-order even expansion but not for convergence. I grepped both pinned cuts, every unique origin tip of main (762), Math- (630) and Universal-Law-Workspace (31), and the tips of the other local repos for these needles: 0.1741, 3.218e, 2.06e-2, I'_k, 0.002723, the comment id 5938972534, s1_root and second_saddle. Every hit was a number that happens to appear in an unrelated JSON or CSV file, with one exception: main origin/claude/nice-maxwell-7i7ok0 (tip 7ce42cadeddeab8445d095907c49adc8e283c1e4) at recovery/session_017Mi3hxjaxV45x6zo6o1ee3/increment2/scratch/c5051/c50_ratio_mc.py, blob 43350fad5fa04be61c1f52205ca64429f10b9fa1 (checked with rev-parse; the branch is not merged into the main cut). That script hard-codes gauss_legendre(16), not 24 nodes. It forms the e^{-12k²}-weighted J_fail sum only as an intermediate it never prints, and it prints only the C_U(1)/C_R ratios. It computes none of I_b, const, ∫A_0 a_fail, the absolute C_R, or #217's I_k and C_fail. Its sibling scripts only check algebraic identities and signs. On the Math- cut, #217's certificate.py certifies I_k with the k^{-5/3} weight, not I'_k. So the cited run is not committed anywhere.

artifacts.statement: ACCEPT of CE-1/CE-2 with new mathematics in Remark 2, which strengthens the CE-2 falsifier. (a) The whole k in [1,2] fiber of the n-th annulus is marked for all |l-l_n| <= l_n^2/4, because r^6 >= l_n^2/4 on the annulus. (b) On J_n the bad density has the closed form nu_beta = 1/r_lo - 1/r_hi, with r_lo^3 = max(l,l_n)/2 and r_hi^3 = min(l,l_n). (c) The good-pair density nu_mu - nu_beta equals l_n^{-1/3} - l^{-1/3} for l >= l_n and 2^{1/3}(l^{-1/3} - l_n^{-1/3}) for l < l_n. By the mean value theorem it is <= l_n^{2/3}/15 on J_n. So mu_good keeps only O(l^{2/3}) of a density of order l^{-1/3}. Remark 1 adds a joint-measurability construction for T^{-1}. Remark 3 gives a unit identification for the applications ([P] (11.2), #243 (4.4), Slice D (D.8)).

Take f in C^5([-1,1]^2) with the pins, M = max_{i+j=5} sup|∂^i_x ∂^j_y f|, 0 < r <= 1/3, |X| <= 3 and rk|ζ| <= 1. Then |(f(rX, rkζ) - b)/(kr^3) - G_k - rG_1| <= M r^2 [17203/(7680k) + (1303/384)|ζ| + (9k/4)ζ^2 + (3k^2/4)|ζ|^3 + (k^3/8)ζ^4 + (k^4/120)|ζ|^5] (B.5). The proof is complete in the post, with explicit pin-coefficient error bounds for δ0 to δ3. The same review also gives cubic-Hermite residual formulas for x^n and minor negative controls. OA-242-B-02 is a growing-jet cubic with physical curvature one inside the rejected interval, and OA-242-E-02 is a correlated-count variance example. These refute unqualified eventwise and calibrated-significance readings.

artifacts.statement: Theorem QSF (v1): for the periodized Gaussian field on R^d/LZ^d, the far-elder lifetime density over separations >=rho satisfies F(ell,rho)<=C_q rho^(-A_N) ell^(q+1), with N=2(q+1) and A_N=24J+12dN+12N(N+1)(d+1), for 0<ell<=rho^2/(64N^2). The proof uses Lemma QJ (lambda_min Cov>=c delta^(24(s-1)) for separated 2-jets). Hence F(ell,ell^beta)=O(ell^q) for beta<=1/A_N, and the same holds for logarithmic cutoffs.

artifacts.statement: Two proof-line obstructions in A2 v1, each with a repair. (1) Lemma 7(b): the exact admissible data psi=1, c=49/100, R=0, eta=1/1000 satisfy (H), with mu=-22201/235298, m_S=599427/21904000 and eps_M=867/15488. There 1-2.048 omega = -11/3125, so the displayed minimum 1.108/(1-2.048 omega) is negative while psi F(M)>0; it is undefined at omega=125/256. Repair: with a=599/250, b=277/250, k=256/125, set K=b+ka=187969/31250=6.015008<6.05 and omega0=a/K=74875/187969, then use b/(1-k omega) for omega<=omega0 and a/omega above it. (2) Lemma 7(c): the segment up to the extra saddle is not in T^v when eta<m. Repair: on Z=tZs with Zs=12 sqrt(1+m), P=-(1+m)(3t^2-2t^3), and the trap segment stops at the unique t_eta in (0,1) with (1+m)(3t_eta^2-2t_eta^3)=1+eta. Sharpness 12 survives as t_eta -> 1. The comment also recommends a Corollary 9(c) domain clarification (empty window for x<=|c|).

artifacts.statement: A review that adds repair mathematics beyond checking. It restates the two Lemma 7 amendments, now with an analytic monotonicity proof of the piecewise bound K=187969/31250 and a nonemptiness proof for the sharpness example (m=1/1000 works, since R<4 and tau<5/6 give m_S>72/3125 and eps_M>9/50). It gives an explicit semialgebraic finite-excursion argument for Proposition 8's path replacement: a polygonal path in the cut complement, finitely many excursions entering and leaving through straight edges, and edge-segment replacement. This supplies the step the source left implicit. Corollary 9(c) domain correction: the typed window |c|<psi<x is empty when x<=|c|; otherwise its exact mass is x^3/3 - c^2 x + 2|c|^3/3, which lies in [0, x^3/3]. The comment also verifies the box constants for Corollary 9(a)-(b).

artifacts.statement: Remark with a new claim and a proof sketch. About M, in polar coordinates rho^2=3s^2+kappa_M Z^2, the cubic is exactly P = -rho^2 + Gamma(theta) rho^3, with an explicit Gamma. For every typed (c,R), including R=0, the degree drop and Delta, the death level is d_P(M) = -4/(27 Gamma*^2), where Gamma* = max_theta Gamma >= 2/(3 sqrt3). The lower bound uses the maximizing ray; the upper bound uses star-shaped superlevel components {rho < rho_1(theta,t)}. Hence elder iff Gamma* = Gamma(0), and rejected mu = 1-4/(27 Gamma*^2). An alternative is also noted: extending the chord ray to the level-mu point (T <= 2/sqrt(1-mu)) makes a mu-only margin sufficient, at a window cost of order (1-c/psi)^(-1/2). Checked numerically on 300 random cases (to 2e-10) and 60 grid maximins (to 9e-5).

artifacts.statement: Feasibility derivation sketch for extending A4 to a compact gap interval K through C103's actual-law inputs. It takes K2(K) = 17/(48k-) + 1/24 + max(1/k-,1,k+)(1+k+)^2/2 and eta_K = 2 K2(K) r w^2, and keeps the LE constant 72. The endpoint conditions are eta_K N<1 and eta_K N(gamma^2+72)<a_M. Splitting at a_M = sqrt(eta_K) and applying squared Markov gives the strip bound C_K[H^3 eta_K + r H^4 sqrt(eta_K)]. The fixed-p replacement of (S20) is C_{K,p}[d + rH^4 + H^3(e/d)^p]. The parameters are alpha=(2-3beta)/16, Lambda=r^-alpha, w=r^(-beta/8), d=r^beta, p >= max(1,(beta+3alpha)/(1-3beta/2)) and integer m >= beta/alpha, with admissibility powers 1-alpha, 1-beta/8, 3/4-beta/8 and 1-beta/4.

lines: It is exactly the condition for the level cubic `{P_QS = −1}` to contain a line through `S`. On `u = 1/2 + mZ` the restriction vanishes iff `ψ + c = 144m²` and `Rq = −48m(ψ − 2c)`, which gives `Rq² = 16(ψ − 2c)²(ψ + c)`.
(S4) is C102 (3.1)–(3.2), extended to `p < 1` by Jensen. (S6) is (1.4), with the Jacobian `r/k⁴` of (4.1). (S7) is (1.8); (S8) is (1.5)–(1.7) and (1.9).

I also checked C102's `|det T_r| = 12r⁻⁵` and target `v_{r,k}`, the pivot identities (4.4), the filtered-determinant bound (4.7) and (6.4). (4.7) is checked rigorously, with rational lower bounds for operator norms.
On 150 exactly pinned degree-5 fields, over five `K` intervals (including `[1/3, 1]`, `[1, 3]` and `[2, 2]`) and `w ∈ {1, 2, 5}`, the largest coefficient-sum ratios are 0.61, 0.61 and 0.62.

The OpenAI review 5968063970 (PASS, no amendment) and this one agree on every item. That includes no extra `k⁴`, the eleven terms of (S27), the 1/4 table, both chord margins, and `α₁ + α₂` (not `α₁ + 2α₂`).

With ρ = r^α and T = r^{−β}, (18) reads r^{9/2−18α−5β} + r^{3/2+mβ/2}, and the §6 cutoff conditions hold for 0 < α, β < 1. So for each fixed α ∈ (0, 1/36) and ε > 0, E[N^p N_R N_far^{r^α}] = O(r^{9/2−18α−ε}); in particular the mixed term is O(r⁴) for every such α. (3) O3: sharper exclusion constants (two-node remainder KR²r²/2, and ψ‴ perturbation constant 19 instead of 28). (4) The exact ψ‴ identity on fields with a known critical graph. (5) The generalized-Rolle step through e = (t²−r²/4)²q. (6) The unit-mass U3 kernel.

artifacts.statement: Corrects the NOTE's claim (frontiers/third_order_coefficient_20261001/NOTE.md lines 319-320 and 339) that the conditional transverse covariance is exactly 2/0/1 at finite separation. For the reference kernel, put Z=f(0) and G=A+ZI. Then Cov(A_ij, f(t,0)) = -delta_ij exp(-t^2/2), so G (GOE 2/0/1) is independent of the whole axial process and, by transverse parity, of the transverse-gradient pins. With sigma_r^2 = Var(f(0)|U_r) > 0, the finite-r pin law therefore has Var(a11|pins) = Var(a22|pins) = 2+sigma_r^2, Cov(a11,a22|pins) = sigma_r^2 and Var(a12|pins) = 1. The midpoint value is not in the span of the pin evaluations: the RKHS function exp(-|x|^2/2)(x_1^2-r^2/4)^2 has zero value and gradient at both pins but a nonzero midpoint value. Also sigma_r^2 = r^8/6144 + O(r^10), from a residual fourth-derivative variance of 24. So 2/0/1 is the contact-limit covariance only. The same review (C129-R1) gives an exact dependent-Bernoulli example: if all 568 indicators equal one Bernoulli(1/100), then (99/100)^568 < 1/40 and (1/100)^568 < 1/40, so the nominal two-sided binomial 95% interval has coverage 0. This shows that aggregate counts alone cannot justify the claimed 'exact 95%' intervals.

A3 v1.1 successor text replacing two Section 4 passages.
(1) (B1) holds on the barrel because D^2_hard f = D^2_hard f(0) + O(r sup|D^3 f|).
(2) The constants are polynomial in R_box, 1/|gamma|, k, 1/lambda_h, 1/min(3,kappa), the three hard cubic jets, and a bound N_f on the derivatives of orders 3-5, where R_box = 3/2 + (5/2)(|gamma|+12)/sqrt(24 lambda~). Also q_0 = O(R_box^2), and the errors are O(r R_box^4).
Obstruction: adding t x1^2 y_h^2/r^2 to an exactly pinned field keeps the pins, the eigenframe and every midpoint jet of order <= 3, yet kr g_zz = -lambda_h + 2tX^2. So for 2 lambda_h/9 <= t < 2 lambda_h the pin curvature keeps its sign while (B1) fails at X=3/2 for every r: fixed midpoint jets do not control the constants. The post states a symbolic check (partial_x partial_h^2 f = 2t/r at S).

artifacts.statement:
A3.1 v1.1 successor text replacing three sentences.
(1) Sharpness of Lemma SR': at E=0 both bounds are sharp as suprema, but they are not sharp jointly in the error budget. P-delta_0 <= g(.,0) <= G <= P+delta_0+(s^2/2)a^T Q^-1 a gives the new bound |e_G| <= delta_0 + s^2 alpha_0^2/(2 Lambda_0), which is strictly below (SR'0) when delta_1 > 0. Example: m=1, Q=1, s=0, eps=1 and E=(1-2z^2)/100 give |e_G| = 1/100, against 13/1200 from (SR'0).
(2) Stationarity Q zeta = s a + E_z gives |zeta| <= (s alpha_0 + delta_1)/Lambda_0, so Lambda_0 can replace Lambda in the middle term of (SR'2). Xi_0 and Xi_2 of Theorem C_d tighten in the same way.
(3) The mixed block of the pin Hessians is of order r^(1/2): for a pinned cubic field it equals exactly r^(1/2) Da_i(M^) = r^(1/2)(-gamma_i/(2k), -beta_i/2), while the determinants move only at order r.
The text also makes FL.4's hypothesis explicit: Psi is injective on W_varpi x B_{R_eta}.

artifacts.statement: A new construction with an argument. It realizes the ordered negative-eigenvalue replacement witness polynomial P_{r,k} of 5999623189 inside the deterministic C^5 torus domain. Take a = min(L/8, 1/4) and an explicit smooth cutoff chi = h(x)h(y)h(z), where h is built from eta(t) = exp(-1/t), equal to 1 on [-a,a]^3 and supported in [-2a,2a]^3. Set F_{r,k} = b + chi(P_{r,k} - b) on the chart and b elsewhere. This is a globally well-defined smooth periodic function. For 0 < r <= a it keeps every pin and midpoint jet: lambda1 = -2r^2 < lambda2 = -r^2 < 0, H_M = diag(-6kr, -r^2, -r^2), H_S = diag(6kr, -r^2, -r^2), W_r/r^4 = 36k^2 r^6 > 0, and model weight (lambda2)_+^2 w = 0. By Leibniz it has the uniform bound ||F_{r,k}||_{C^5} <= C_L(1+|b|+k_+) =: N_*. So for r <= r_* = min(a, 1, 1/(2N_*)) one has r||F||_{C^5} <= 1/2. The result is an in-domain deterministic family with negative lambda2 and positive actual typed weight, consistent with W3 and not a counterexample to it.

artifacts.statement: Author-side supporting lemma for LM006's Q_L condition. It assumes a positive exact lattice spectral representation K(z)=sum_k p_k exp(i nu k.z) with nu=2pi/L and pins J=(f,fx,fy,fxx,fxy,fxxx), Q=fyy at one point. Strip the column factors and evaluate the polynomial columns (1,x,y,x^2,xy,x^3,y^2) at the nodes (0,0),(1,0),(-1,0),(2,0),(0,1),(0,-1),(1,1). The resulting 7x7 integer matrix has exact determinant 24, so the joint seven-functional covariance is positive definite and the six-pin covariance is invertible. A Schur floor follows: the finite-difference row (-1,0,0,0,1/2,1/2,0) has squared norm 3/2 and gives -R(0,0)+(R(0,1)+R(0,-1))/2=-nu^2, so by Cauchy-Schwarz Var(Q|J) >= (2/3) p_* nu^4 > 0, where p_*=min(p_(0,0),p_(0,1),p_(0,-1)). The comment also reports exact Fraction checks. I re-verified det=24, row*M=e_7 and norm^2=3/2 exactly.

artifacts.statement: Counterexample to review 6006807347 §3, which claimed that Delta = m6 - m4^2/m2 > 0 is strict in the same cases as m4 > m2^2. The law P(X=0)=1/2, P(X=+-1)=1/4 has m2=m4=m6=1/2, so m4-m2^2 = 1/4 > 0, yet Delta = 0 because X^3=X a.s. Correct characterization: for m2>0 and a finite sixth moment, Delta = E[(X^3-(m4/m2)X)^2], so Delta=0 iff the law is supported in {0,-a,a} for some a>0. Two distinct nonzero absolute values with positive mass suffice for Delta>0.

artifacts.statement: QS addendum A3.8, d=3 failure-measure rate on the growing soft layer D_Lambda={|lambda~|<=Lambda}, delivered in full inline. It has Lemmas 1.1-1.3 (layer law with explicit H=1+Lambda dependence), 2.1-2.4 (edges, radius tails, hard-gap strip, Hessian transfer), 3.1-3.2 (correlated and decision bands with a shell cutoff), 4.1-4.2 (margins, endpoint strip), 5.1-5.4 (actual and model failure tails, polynomial and exponential; P_QS facts psi^3<=64|c|^3+2R^2 on Rsec^(inf); coefficient bracket 0<M_*<=alpha^(3)<=M^*), and Proposition 6.1 (layer comparison with ledger Rerr3). Theorem QFE3: for every beta<2/3, ||nu_r^F-nu_0^F||_var<=C_beta r^beta and 1-p_r=r^3 alpha^(3)+O_beta(r^(3+beta)), using the schedule alpha=(2-3beta)/16, Lambda=r^-alpha, w=r^(-beta/8). Theorem ER3: the endpoint ||nu_r^F-nu_0^F||_var<=C r^(2/3) log(1/r)^(8/3), so 1-p_r=r^3 alpha^(3)+O(r^(11/3) log(1/r)^(8/3)). Here alpha^(3)=m_R^(inf)/z_0 is an explicit Gaussian integral over the Lambda-free rejected sector, and the bounds are uniform over b in B_0, k in [k-,k+] and the frame. All proofs are given.

artifacts.statement: Elementary lemma with proof by cases (U<=1 and U>=1): for U>=0, U^8 <= 1 + U^9. Hence aU^9 + bU^8 <= (a+b)U^9 + b for a,b,U>=0. Consequence: with only nonnegative residual support, i.e. without j>=1, the R19/R18 outer envelope is bounded by pi*C0*A*r^5*[256*(a+b)*(M9*G2 + m*G11) + b*m*G2], where a=D^3/3 and b=E*D^2/2. Under j>=1 the extra b*m*G2 term is unnecessary. Two finite counterexamples come with it: a unit-mass atom at j=0 shows that mass 1 does not give unit support, and m=512 delta_0 shows that m cannot silently be set to 1.

artifacts.statement: Full-field Monte Carlo of the superlevel H0 persistence of the periodized field e^{-|z|^2/2}: d=2 uses 4000 fields of side 64; d=3 uses 2992 of 3000 retained fields of side 16 on a 256^3 grid. The counts are compared with the parameter-free three-term law and with C7's four-term law at the model coefficient (J/30 - I~) S_d, which is 0.0774672 in d=3 and 0.0615684 in d=2. On [1e-4, 3e-2], chi^2 drops from 84 to 23 (d=3) and from 44 to 7 (d=2). A free l^{2/3} fit gives 0.060+/-0.007 (d=3) and 0.054+/-0.009 (d=2), and the next-order k l^{3/4} fit gives about -0.024+/-0.010 (d=3). The post also gives exploration values D=0.0767381 (two quadratures) and J=4.1977819815839, and defines the model number D (request 1: certify D).

- The blinded coefficient test was NOT_RUN.

Then there exist k <= n, a continuous linear equivalence P : EuclideanSpace(Fin n) ≃L Fin n -> R, an open V containing J = signSym n k, a C2 branch s with s(J)=0, and an OpenPartialHomeomorph e with e(u) = Theta(u) = (I + J*s(M u))u, where M = TaylorSymLift.sourceSymMatrix omega x0 P and M 0 = J. Also e 0 = 0, e.symm 0 = 0, 0 lies in both domains, DTheta(0) = Id, and e is C2 on its source and its inverse C2 on its target. The energy identities are F(x0+Pu) = F(x0) + quadratic J (e u) on e.source and F(x0+P(e.symm v)) = F(x0) + quadratic J v on e.target. artifacts.statement: AMEND_SCOPE_NOTE review of the OPEN RN near-pin witness-collision target. It adds a small new counting lemma with a one-line proof. Let A be the finite set of ordered window pairs whose first witness is near a pin, and B the set whose second witness is near. Swapping labels gives |A| = |B|, so |A| <= |A ∪ B| <= 2|A|. Hence an O(r^3) bound on nearPinPairCount (first-near only) is order-equivalent, up to a constant at most 2, to the source's at-least-one-witness count. The review also corrects the existing docstring, which wrongly said second-only pairs are counted 'by symmetry only when both are near'; they are in fact counted through their swapped ordered mate. Two scope caveats go with it: the planar D5 section 5 source versus the target's general d >= 2, and the fact that Set.ncard = 0 on infinite sets lets the expected count vanish spuriously unless almost-sure finiteness or measurability is supplied. The lemma is minor.

artifacts.statement: Setting: quotient torus X = R^d/(L Z^d), d>=2, L>0, descended smooth periodic g with nondegenerate critical points and distinct critical values; M a nonessential nondegenerate local maximum, b=g(M), delta=I.deathHeight(g,M); C(h,M) for h<=b means there is a path from M to some y with g(y)>b inside the closed superlevel {g>=h}. Target: (1) delta<b and delta is an attained critical value; (2) C(h,M) iff h<=delta, including h=delta; (3) the unique torus critical point S with g(S)=delta has Morse index d-1 and merges the b-labelled component with a strictly older-labelled one; (4) this matches I.ElderPartner g M S through quotient/lift compatibility. The comment's own nonauthor review adds a conditional derivation sketch ('Reconstruction of the intended mathematical obligation'). It covers: nonemptiness and boundedness of the bottleneck family from compactness and path-connectedness. It gets delta<b from an isolating neighbourhood of the nondegenerate maximum whose boundary lies uniformly below b. It uses finiteness of the compact Morse critical set and an elder-label induction (keep the higher birth label when components merge; handles inside one component do not change labels). It argues that only an index-one handle for -g (g-index d-1) can merge components. It then proves both directions of the equivalence: for h<delta the strict clause gives a witness, h=delta uses the closed critical-level theorem, and for h>delta any closed witness would be a strict witness at some k with delta<k<h, a contradiction. A boundary and negative-control table checks h=b, delta<h<b, h=delta, h<delta, and h>b. It includes the order-theoretic countercontrol: the bottleneck set {delta-1/n} has supremum delta but no witness attaining the endpoint. It also treats the essential maximum, nonmerging saddles, earlier younger mergers, repeated Euclidean lifts, and the label interval (delta,b], equivalently [-b,-delta) in t=-h.

artifacts.statement: Explicit counterexamples bounding the C263 strict-clearance cut. (1) Continuity cannot be dropped: on R take g(x)=1 for x<=0, g(x)=x for 0<x<1 and g(x)=2 for x>=1, with M=0. By the IVT, every path to y>=1 passes through x=min(h/2,1/2), so C=(-inf,0] and D=0. Hence 0 is in C with no larger member, and both strict improvement and the strict cut fail. (2) Constant g=-1 gives C empty and D=0, which refutes D<=g(M); at h=-1, h<D holds with h not in C, so the nonessential guard of the cut is necessary. (3) For continuous nonessential g, the attained minimum on the witness path gives the midpoint improvement, so D is not in C and h<=D cannot replace h<D. (4) The reviewer adds that g(x)=x with M=0 gives C=(-inf,0) and D=g(M)=0, so a strict bound D<g(M) is false in general. The comment also gives a proposed 11-line Lean false control (FALSE_CONTROL_PROPOSAL.lean, sha 771c4433...) for the unguarded bound.

artifacts.statement: Exact elementary controls for the backward-heat fold and ordinary sublevel H0 on a finite interval. (1) Exact fold H_t=z^2+1-2t, F_t=z^3/3-(2t-1)z, s=sqrt(2t-1): on [-L,L] with L>2s the left endpoint component is older, the minimum at s dies at the maximum at -s, and the finite bar is ell=4s^3/3=r^3/6 with r=2s. (2) Boundary countercontrol: at s=1, L=3/2 the critical-value gap is still 4/3 but the finite bar is born at the left boundary and has length 7/24, while at L=3 the bar is 4/3, from exact rational evaluation. (3) Information-loss counterexample: H=1 and H=z^2+1 at t=0 both have increasing primitives and no finite bars, though the second has nonreal zeros. On [-L,L], H=1+L^2/3 matches that primitive's endpoint values, so interval barcodes cannot certify that complex zeros are real. (4) Degeneracy: H=x^3-6tx gives a triple collision with adjacent primitive barrier 9t^2=r^4/4 for r=sqrt(6t), so the double-zero cubic hypothesis is essential. The local Taylor normal form H=A(x^2-2tau)+..., with r~2sqrt(2tau) and ell~|A|r^3/6, is restated with its remainder hypotheses left separate.

artifacts.statement: Shows that a finite ordinary marginal negative mark moment does not give the short-bar density exponent; the moment has to be taken under the limiting collision-mark measure with the D1 joint-law, envelope and selection hypotheses. Example: if r has density 3r^2 on (0,1), k=r and ell = k r^3 = r^4, then E[k^-1] = 3/2 is finite, yet the exact lifetime density is (3/4) ell^(-1/4), not ell^0. This is stated as consistent with D1, which keeps those hypotheses.

artifacts.statement: Counterexample to the packet claim (README lines 420-424, 833-836 at 70f3d993) that any positive C1 weight w gives ell_w = w(x0) ell (1+O(r^2)). Take H(t,x)=x^2-2t, a=sqrt(2t), r=2a, and w(x)=1+|x|^(1+eta) with 0<eta<1, a fixed positive C1 weight. Direct integration gives ell = 4a^3/3 and ell_w/ell = 1 + 3a^(1+eta)/((2+eta)(4+eta)); for eta=1/2 the excess is (4/15)a^(3/2), so the relative correction is not O(r^2). On a fixed interval around the window both quantities are actual bars for small a. Suggested repair: require bounded second derivative (C^{1,1}) plus controlled fold asymmetry, or weaken the error term; ensemble transfer also needs uniform weight and marked-measure hypotheses. (I re-derived the ratio and the 4/15 value myself; both are correct.)

artifacts.statement: Repair of the local-persistence argument (packet Proposition 1(c), README lines 262-294). First, complete the domain: a compact interval I inside the analytic domain, a base point z* in I, a fixed field, and the superlevel convention. Then the elder argument for A>0: the local maximum's component is trapped inside W above the local minimum, while the component through the right side already contains a strictly higher value, so it kills the new younger bar at the local minimum. For A<0, simply replacing H by -H would swap superlevel and sublevel persistence. Instead use the left-side argument, or the simultaneous reflection H(t,x) -> -H(t,-x), F(t,x) -> F(t,-x), which preserves superlevels. The result is a local bar for small tau on a fixed surrounding interval, not for arbitrary close pairs or pairing at t=0. Also corrects the exact equality r^2 = 8 tau to r^2 = 8 tau (1+O(tau)). artifacts.statement: Deduction, with a proof sketch, from existing global estimates. Polymath15 Theorem 1.5(i) gives an absolute C such that for 0<t<=1/2 every zero of H_t with real part >= exp(C/t) is real. If Lambda>0 this is uniform on [Lambda/2, Lambda]. With symmetry and the strip bound, nonreal roots at t_n increasing to Lambda stay in a fixed compact set, and a subsequence converges to a real zero of H_Lambda. If that zero were simple, real-analytic continuation would keep nearby roots real, a contradiction. So Lambda>0 forces a multiple real zero of H_Lambda at finite height. Limits stated: its multiplicity may exceed 2, so it need not be a nondegenerate fold; there is no compact bound at Lambda=0 because exp(C/t) diverges; this is not an RH result. The review labels it an informational classical clarification, not a new RH result.

artifacts.statement: Theorem (general amplitude-mixture law). Let H be SG-admitted on the flat torus, A > 0 independent of H with any law, F = A*H and m = E[A^(-2/3)]. (1) COUNT in all consumed forms, CONTACT and SELECT hold for every A. (2) ENVELOPE holds iff m < infinity, with H^F = E[A^-2 H_SG(b/A,k/A)] and its k^(-2/3)-mass equal to m times SG's. (3) If m < infinity then FAR holds, nu_F(l) ~ m*C_H*l^(-1/3) and E N^F_t/V ~ (3/2) m C_H t^(2/3). (4) If m = infinity then l^(1/3) nu_F(l) -> infinity. So the -1/3 law holds exactly when E[A^(-2/3)] < infinity, with coefficient E[A^(-2/3)] C_H. For the PR's power law this is alpha > 2/3 with m = a^(-2/3) alpha/(alpha - 2/3), which reproduces (16). The proof skeleton uses the identities B^F_r = E[A^-2 B^H_r(b/A,k/A)] and nu_F(l) = E[A^-1 nu_H(l/A)], dominated convergence and Fatou, and re-derives SG's far bound for all u > 0. The qualifications and the non-covered cases are stated.

artifacts.statement: General amplitude-mixture law, v1.1, offered as a corollary of the contract classification 6140734834. Setup: H is an SG-admitted field on the flat torus, A is a (0,inf)-valued variable independent of H with any law, F = A·H and m = E[A^(-2/3)]. (1) COUNT (in the forms the structural theorem consumes), CONTACT and SELECT hold for every such A. (2) ENVELOPE holds iff m < inf, with envelope H^F(b,k) = E[A^-2 H_SG(b/A,k/A)] and k^(-2/3)-mass equal to m times SG's. If m = inf, the weighted mass of the contact limit is 3 m c_q = inf. (3) If m < inf, FAR holds, nu_F(l) ~ m C_H l^(-1/3) and E N^F_t/V ~ (3/2) m C_H t^(2/3). This follows from the transform nu_F(l) = E[A^-1 nu_H(l/A)] by dominated convergence with dominator G·A^(-2/3). (4) If m = inf, then l^(1/3) nu_F -> inf and t^(-2/3) m_F -> inf, by Fatou. Hence the -1/3 law holds exactly when E[A^(-2/3)] < inf, with coefficient E[A^(-2/3)] C_H. For this PR's power law the condition is alpha > 2/3. The proof skeleton covers the scaling identity under conditioning on A=s, the mixing identities for B^F_r, K^F, nu_F and m_F, the change of variables with Tonelli, and dominated convergence and Fatou. It re-derives the far bound nu_(H,far)(u) <= C(1+u)^(2d) e^(-c u^2) for all u > 0 from SG's separated-pair argument. The post also lists qualifications and numerical sanity checks.

artifacts.statement: Explicit reduction of the D2 two-mass moment floors to the scalar Schur-complement residual. With Y=X^2, law nu and weight w>=0, let Q_w(nu)=int w [[1,y],[y,y^2]] dnu = [[alpha,beta],[beta,gamma]] with alpha>0. Then Phi(Q_w) = gamma-beta^2/alpha = inf_c int w(y)(y-c)^2 dnu. If nu>=nu0 as nonnegative measures, the residual dominates for every c, so Phi is monotone (equivalently Q_w(nu)-Q_w(nu0) is PSD), and nu0 must not be renormalized. For nu0 = p delta_u + q delta_v, the w=1 row gives retained residual pq(u-v)^2/(p+q) against g = E[Y^2]-E[Y]^2. The w=y row gives (pu)(qv)(u-v)^2/(pu+qv) against Delta = E[Y^3]-E[Y^2]^2/E[Y]. Also E[Y]>=pu+qv. For a finite measure of mass M the first residual is int Y^2 - (int Y)^2/M. The comment also explains the directional bound S(theta)=N/D(theta) >= min(N/D0,N/D1) >= min(g0, 2 s0^2), which needs no upper-moment input. Exact Fraction examples at (p,q,u,v)=(1/5,1/3,2,5) give floors (31/15, 9/8, 90/31) and two boundary remainders. A non-probability measure 2 delta_1 has raw gap -2 but mass-normalized residual 0.

artifacts.statement: Derives the S8 opening normalization in finite dimensions. The pin transform in coordinates (f(M),f(S),fx(M),fx(S)) is block lower triangular: the height block has determinant 1/r, the derivative block [-1/r,1/r;6/r^2,6/r^2] has determinant -12/r^3, and each of the d-1 transverse blocks has determinant 1/r. So the absolute determinant is 12 r^-(d+3). The explicit cubic h(x)=b-kr^3/2-(3/2)kr^2 x+2kx^3 realizes the pins, with h'''=12k and endpoint h''=-+6kr. From H=D_r K D_r, det H = r det K. The polar, pin and Hessian powers combine to r^(d-1) r^-(d+3) r^2 = r^-2, and dell=r^3 dk accounts for the marked factor. Correction: k=ell/r^3 has signed derivative dk/dr=-3ell/r^4, not a positive one, so the endpoints must be reversed to get int_0^inf r^-2 A0(ell/r^3) dr = ell^(-1/3) int_0^inf A0(k)/(3k^(2/3)) dk. Likewise (b,ell)->(b,b-ell) has signed determinant -1 and absolute Jacobian 1. Proposed wording: |dk/dr|=3 ell r^-4, plus 'absolute Jacobian one'.

artifacts.statement: For real w,h,u,v with D-=w-h+u and D+=w+h+v, the identity D-D+ = [w+(u+v)/2]^2 - [h+(v-u)/2]^2 holds exactly. So if |u|+|v|<=eps, then [-D-D+]_+ <= (|h|+eps/2)^2 <= 2h^2+eps^2/2. The first bound is sharp: take w=0, u=-s eps/2, v=s eps/2 with s=sign(h). Substituting h=6k Delta, w=rY, u=R_M, v=R_S and the manuscript's assumed residual bound eps=C0 r^2(1+k)T^N1 gives W_r/r^2 <= 72k^2 Delta^2 + (C0^2/2) r^4(1+k)^2 T^(2N1), which also holds at k=0. Two counterexamples show the premises cannot be weakened: with a non-common shift (w-=r, w+=-r) the negative product is r^2, not O(r^4); without sign selection, w=1 and h=u=v=0 gives an absolute product of 1 against a bound of 0.

artifacts.statement: A new matrix-analysis lemma with proof. For real symmetric d x d matrices, define F_j(A)=|det A| if A is nonsingular of index j, and 0 otherwise. Then |F_j(A)-F_j(B)| <= d R^(d-1) ||A-B||op with R=max(||A||op,||B||op). The proof integrates along a segment, using multilinearity and the column-volume bound, and holds even at singular matrices. The constant is sharp (A=RS, B=(R-h)S), so d>=2 has no global Lipschitz constant. The post also derives a pair-product bound |F_jF_k-F_j'F_k'| <= d R^(2d-1) Delta, and a Holder expectation bound E|...| <= d ||R||_{L^2d}^(2d-1) ||Delta||_{L^2d}. A finite-mixture counterexample (A_n=-nI, B_n=n diag(-1,...,-1,1) with probability n^(-2d)) shows that convergence in probability with bounded E R^(2d) does not suffice. An inline exact-Fraction diagnostic is included, with deliberately false variants.

The conditioning set is P=(f,f_t,f_tt,f_ttt,f_v,f_tv,f_w,f_tw). The residual Gram matrix is diag(2,6,120,2,24,2,1,2). artifacts.statement: Full conventional proof note in 10 sections, 'Higher configurations for the normalized Gaussian square truncations'. (i) New constructive Euclidean full-jet floor. For p points in R^2 with minimum separation 0<eta<=1, the covariance of all 10p raw derivatives of order <=3 of the field with covariance exp(-|h|^2/2) is >= c_p eta^(8p-2) I. The proof uses explicit Hermite-interpolation duals g_{i,beta} and a submultiplicative eta-norm coefficient bound (3/2)21096^(p-1), and c_p is explicit and does not depend on the diameter. After symmetric-tensor weighting, the 7p contact covariance is >= (c_p/2) eta^(8p-2) I for arbitrary frames. (ii) Torus clustering/lifting transfer to the declared normalized truncation family (1), with L t^(1/3)->ell_*: a uniform floor m_p(t)=c''_p eta^(8p-2), via Weyl's inequality and Delta_t=o(eta^(nu_p)). (iii) Fixed-p 6p-pin kernel bounds, using the regular divided-difference rows and the canonical conditional coupling: |K_p^r|<=C_p m^(-7p) and |K_p^r-K_p^0|<=C_p sqrt(r) m^(-(7p+2)). (iv) Near configurations, including shared endpoints, with a p-dependent cutoff eta_p=c/H_p(t), giving expected near count <=C 16^(2p) t^4. Middle configurations are O_p(t^(2/3) log(1/t)^(1+7p(8p-2))). Far configurations factor with error C_p[d_t(R_t)+sqrt(r_t)]. (v) Compact one-point intensity nu = v_* 144 s^(-1/3) k^(4/3) A^2 p_Jinf,u(b,0,0,12k,0,0,A), with ordered factorial-moment convergence (4) for C_c(E) tests and all compact Laplace functionals (5) by Bonferroni. These give vague convergence of the local endpoint-candidate process to a Poisson process with intensity (3), for this one specified changing Gaussian law (not global persistence bars or arbitrary spectra).

artifacts.statement: Nonauthor review (ACCEPT_SCOPED) of the frozen asymmetric elder trap proposal. The new mathematics is the reviewer's join of the proposal's conditional candidate-process input to the accepted higher-configuration Gaussian theorem. For the one declared ideal finite Gaussian truncation family, take the uniform good norm event G_Q, with Q_p chosen so that K^(4p)(1+L)^2 exp[-Q_p/(16T)] = t^u0. On that event every candidate in a fixed compact regular-mark window passes the trap and the intrinsic Borel selector, so the elder-selected sector Y_t equals the regular candidate sector. The Laplace discrepancy is bounded by P(bad event). The fixed-p ordered factorial discrepancy is bounded by the product of sup norms times (16K^2)^(2p) P(bad). Hence the accepted compact regular-mark Poisson (intensity coefficient 144) Laplace/vague conclusions and every fixed-order factorial conclusion transfer to Y_t. The review also re-derives the proposal's supporting steps in full in its own words: the strip boundary bounds m-f(-R) >= tau R^3/12 and f(R)-d >= tau R^3/96, with boundary(D) meeting {F>=d} only at S; clopen separation giving a global first elder death with strict clearance (-inf,d) and attainment at d; the ordinary-H0 interval direct summand on (d,m], with explicit section [M]-[P], indicator retraction and all naturality squares; the eigenframe cubic error 3B^2 r/a; W^2 <= Q on G_Q; and R >= kappa/Q. It adds its own exact controls (81 polynomial traps, 72 norm-constant sets, 288 radius ledgers, signed-subset factorial comparisons, 36 cover/count cancellations) with four rejected negative controls, and it keeps the false full-boundary height barrier as a counterexample. Not established: a simultaneous or exhaustive decomposition, all-bar reverse regularity, singular/unbounded mark tightness, or the full unmarked bar law.

artifacts.statement: Exact analytic counterexample to the literal domain of TECHNICAL_METHOD_V1, M14/M15. V1's moment-tail bound S_k - S_k^(M) <= 2h^(2k) I_k(M;alpha) is stated for real M>0 with M>=sqrt(k/alpha). It fails for non-integer M. Take k=0, alpha=1, M=9/10: the finite sum keeps only m=0, so both the +1 and -1 modes are omitted and the tail is at least 2e^-1. The claimed M14/M15 upper bound is (10/9)e^(-81/100), which is less than 2e^-1 because e^(19/100) <= 100/81 < 9/5. No numerics are used. Consequence: the spectral cutoff M must be a positive integer.

artifacts.statement: Quantitative cone-moment perturbation lemma (P3), with a full proof. Let F(Gamma)=E[w(T(Gamma^(1/2)Z))] with w(A)=(det A)^2 1{A<0}. If gamma I <= Gamma, Gamma' <= Lambda I and ||Gamma-Gamma'||_op <= delta, then |F(Gamma)-F(Gamma')| <= K_F delta, where K_F = n 2^n Lambda^(n-1/2) gamma^(-1/2) M_(N,n) and M_(N,n) = prod_{j<n}(N+2j). The proof writes S-S' as the solution of the Sylvester equation, X = integral_0^inf exp(-tS)(Gamma-Gamma')exp(-tS')dt, so ||S-S'||_op <= delta/(2 sqrt(gamma)) for non-commuting Gamma, Gamma'. It then couples both matrices to the same Z and applies M20. artifacts.statement: Complete unchanged copy of the 5032-byte appendix 'Independent finite smooth incidence reconstruction' (17 Oct 2026). (1) Proves equal-dimensional smooth Sard by a cube-covering and Taylor-remainder argument. (2) Proves the Borel weighted equal-dimensional area formula, integral h|det DPhi| dz = integral sum over Phi^-1(y) of h dy, for nonnegative Borel h, via IFT pieces, monotone limits and Tonelli. (3) Parameterizes the critical-point incidence as (p,eta) -> (a(p,eta),eta) with a = -B(p)^-1(grad T + D(p)eta). Its Jacobian is |det H|/|det B|; for two sites it is |det H_p det H_q|/|det B_pair|. The minor denominator then cancels to give the Gaussian observation density, with one Hessian determinant at each root. (4) Shows the marks may be any nonnegative Borel function, including a nonlocal elder-bar indicator. (5) States that literal-target fiber identification remains a separate Gaussian calculation.

artifacts.statement: Rounding-soundness read of the H3 band v2 certificate (PR #447 head 6651242a). R2 rigor gap: majA and majGY form their Cauchy-majorant ratio as 1/RHO in round-to-nearest mp. An exact Fraction check shows 1/RHO lies below the exact 1/rho_b (rho_b = the binary value of mpf('0.11')) by a relative 1.97e-102, so for j>N the claimed tail majorant C*q^j falls short of M*rho_b^-j by a relative factor of about j*2e-102. These tails feed MT/ST on the first cell. Repair: up(1/RHOi), checked to be >= 1/rho_b, at both call sites. Both envelopes then pass with byte-identical transcripts, so no printed bound changes. Also: directed-rounding replays (round down 'f' and up 'c') reproduce every CERT line and every 20-digit per-cell value. Law containment, which CB7 checks only at r=1/20, is extended to 26 r values across every cell: all 42 mu/Sigma entries lie inside both the cell and point enclosures, with minimum slack 2.2e-93 (point) and 7.5e-90 (cell), against a direct-law error <=4.7e-198. Non-certifying Monte Carlo puts E[G_r] near 3.2354 and 3.2282. R1 is an unguarded tail_from branch (robustness note only).

artifacts.statement: Frozen PAPER_JUSTIFICATION.md (12801B, sha256 9049bf47...7021). Theorem: let d be any dimension, L>0, g:E d->R L-periodic and a any real. If {x | a<=g x} is locally path connected, then the torus-quotient closed superlevel {q | a<=descendedHeight g q} is locally path connected. The proof has four steps. (1) torus_proj is an open quotient map: it is surjective, continuous, and open because it is a covering. (2) The preimage of the quotient superlevel is exactly the Euclidean superlevel, via descendedHeight_proj. (3) Restricting an open quotient map over an arbitrary target subset, closed or not, gives an open quotient map. (4) LPC descends along quotient maps. A consumer lemma then replaces the quotient-LPC premise of quotient_death_attainment with Euclidean LPC at the unchanged death height. The comment also includes the intentionally failing negative fixture OmittedEuclideanLPC.lean.

With delta=sqrt(2pi)(p-1/2), F(delta)=Psi(p) exactly, because the numerator and denominator phase shifts cancel. Also F^(k)(delta)=(2pi)^(-k/2)Psi^(k)(p), and C_k(packet)=C_k(Siegel)/(2pi)^(k/2). artifacts.statement: Two explicit counterexamples, inside a C257 literal-hypothesis audit, that block broadening the scope. (1) On the circle of period 2pi, take g(x)=cos x and the regular nonglobal point M=pi/2. g is smooth, periodic and Morse with distinct critical values, yet the strict-clearance threshold is delta=0=b. So strict death drop (delta<b) cannot follow from the arbitrary-M hypotheses of the R3 public attainment signature; it needs M to be a local maximum. (2) Take d=1, L=0, g(x)=x^2. IsLPeriodic is vacuous, the only critical point 0 has a nondegenerate Hessian and distinct critical values hold, but there is no global maximum. So the bare literal IsSmooth/IsLPeriodic/IsMorseDistinct predicates without L>0 do not give the compact-maxima conclusion. The audit also lists the literal-to-geometric bridge obligations that remain open: positivity of the literal infimum torusDist for distinct quotient points, HessianHasInertia without orthogonality, the match of the intrinsic delta with the C263 superlevelBar_deathHeight, and the gap between R3's older-critical endpoint and C256's fixed-older-maximum result.

Definitions: restrictCovector, ridgeAddition, negativePartialGradient, negativeHessianBlock. Theorems with full proofs: negativeHessianBlock_apply; negativeHessianBlock_isInvertible (negative definiteness of the Hessian on V gives an invertible block, including V = 0); negativePartialGradient_contDiff (C^2); negativePartialGradient_hasFDerivAt; and the main result exists_negative_partial_gradient_ridge. The main result states that for smooth f, a critical point p, and V with hessian(v,v) < 0 for v != 0, there is r : E d -> V with r 0 = 0, ContDiffAt 2 at 0, the eventual equation fderiv f (p + w + r w) z = 0 for all z in V, and the differentiated equation hessian(w + Dr(0) w, z) = 0, proved by the implicit function theorem. The module formalizes only the partial-gradient IFT step of the direct-ridge paper at Math-#487/6292079965.

The proof uses a nonzero polynomial vanishing on the graph, factors out y^j, writes A(h)=Q(h,0)=h^m a(h), and applies a mean-value bound with M=1+max|d_yQ|; no continuity of f is needed. (2) If f is also nondecreasing, then f>=c* h^m on all of (0,h0] with c*=min(c0, f(h1)/h0^m). (3) Applied to the nested slices D_eta={|t|,|n|>=eta}, the infimum f(eta)=inf kappa is nondecreasing, so q(eta)=f/2>=(c*/2) eta^m. artifacts.statement: Writes out the missing joint-limit step for the band liminf lower bound. For distinct annulus points x,y the joint vector consists of the divided pin rows, the scaled pin Hessians, grad F(x), grad F(y), H(x) and H(y). Its covariance converges as r->0 to the covariance of non-duplicated jets at {0,x,y}. Finite-jet positivity makes that limit positive definite. Continuity of Gaussian regression then gives pointwise convergence of the conditional density and of the typed-weight conditional expectation, because the boundary of the type event is null; bounded convergence applies after truncation. Dividing by Z_r/r^2->z_0>0 gives pointwise convergence of the normalised integrand, and Fatou's lemma then gives the liminf lower bound without uniform integrability.

artifacts.statement: Route obstruction: the existing off-axis target-gap / angular-shell route gives no domination uniform as k->0. With the k-dependence restored, E>=c k^2/(H^2+r^2), and J_r(h,k)<=C r h^-2 exp(-c k^2/h^2) when r<=a h^4. The dyadic sum has envelope asymptotic to k^-2, so N_good<=C r^5(1+k^-2), and the peak shell is in the refined regime only if k>~r^{1/4}. The thin-set fallback C r^-63 exp(-c k^2 r^-1/2) is O(r^5) under the sufficient cutoff k>~r^{1/4} sqrt(log(1/r)). At k=0 every exceptional-direction gap vanishes, so continuity cannot repair the route. The smallest corrected statement is N_off<=C r^5(1+kappa(r)^-2) for kappa(r)>=C r^{1/4} sqrt(log(1/r)). An all-mark measure needs integral m(k) k^-2 dk<infinity, so m=O(k^alpha) suffices only for alpha>1.

artifacts.statement: Short derivations for the Env8 T-conditional Hessian envelope. (1) A cheap constant bound Env8 <= C, from sigma_i <= unconditional SD = O(1) and |mu_i| <= |d2P_nu| + sqrt(Var R_H)·sqrt(E_T) with E_T <= C. This bound loses the small factors the band needs (det H(pin)=O(rs), H(x)=O(s), |H(x)w|=O(e)). (2) The divided-difference row (∇F(y)-∇F(x))/η = H_x w + (η/2)D^3F[w,w] + ..., when set to zero, forces H_x w = O(η) in conditional L2. det H_x then splits through (H_x w) and (H_x w^⊥) over |w|^2, so one factor is O(e); the same holds for H_y. (3) A heuristic expectation that the pin pair's conditional SD must be computed jointly with the witness rows as q->0.

artifacts.statement: Explicit counterexample to identifying LM002 quartic endpoint matrices with literal endpoint Hessians. The smooth perturbation x^5(x^2-r^2/4)^2 leaves the pins unchanged (it has a double zero at x=±r/2) and leaves the midpoint derivatives unchanged (all derivatives through order 4 vanish at 0). It does change the endpoint xx second derivative (it equals 8x^7 = ±r^7/16 at ±r/2). So the GP-DER-043 quartic matrices cannot be identified with arbitrary literal endpoint Hessians. The repair route is the actual six-vector (fxx(M)/r, fxy(M)/r, fyy(M), fxx(S)/r, fxy(S)/r, fyy(S)) of GP-DER-047 §13.

artifacts.statement: Two elementary derivations. First, the Whitney fold normal form F=c^(-1)(½xᵀAx+z³/3-λz) has critical points at z=±√λ, separation r=2√λ and critical-value gap 4λ^(3/2)/(3c)=r³/(6c), so the collision order is m=3. Second, if the selected-pair shell intensity is A r^α dr and ℓ=c r^m, then a change of variables gives dN/dℓ=(A/m)c^(-(α+1)/m) ℓ^((α+1)/m-1). So DP-05's exponent is an elementary pushforward identity that holds only conditionally on both hypotheses, and it is not a universality theorem.
